title: SphericalRandomUtility.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Minimize a real-valued function convex on the closed Euclidean ball of radius R centered at zero. Convexity is required only on the feasible ball, and the objective may be nonsmooth.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: A query selects two feasible points x and y. The oracle returns one bit, true exactly when f(y)+⟨Z,y⟩ ≤ f(x)+⟨Z,x⟩. Both utilities use the same hidden draw Z, so the noise in their difference is ⟨Z,x−y⟩. Ties return true. The algorithm receives only the bit and may choose the next pair adaptively.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SphericalRandomUtility.lean, sampleUtility, comparePair, spec.Query, spec.Reply and spec.admissible. LongTails/Template.lean, Algorithm.query and Algorithm.update.

distinctive_assumptions.label: heavy_tailed_noise
distinctive_assumptions.details: With probability at least 1/2 over Z, the entire sample utility x ↦ f(x)+⟨Z,x⟩ is B-Lipschitz on the feasible ball, simultaneously for all pairs. This quantile condition permits perturbation laws with infinite moments.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SphericalRandomUtility.lean, good, sampleUtility and the half-mass condition in spec.admissible.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is Euclidean ℝᵈ with d ≥ 2. The public parameters are d, R, B and ε, with R > 0, B > 0 and 0 < ε ≤ BR/16.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SphericalRandomUtility.lean, Point, Params, Feasible, spec.publicInput and spec.valid.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The hidden perturbation law is invariant under every orthogonal transformation. Successive query perturbations are independent with this same marginal law. The comparison map is jointly measurable in the queried pair and the perturbation.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SphericalRandomUtility.lean, Spherical and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean, IID.measurable, IID.independent and IID.marginal.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: Return a feasible point x̂. The gap is f(x̂)−f(x⋆), where x⋆ attains the minimum of f on the same closed ball.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The output gap must be integrable and satisfy E[f(x̂)−f(x⋆)] ≤ ε. The expectation includes the algorithm seed and the independent oracle sequence under a fixed cap on comparison calls.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: Each comparison uses a shared spherical random linear perturbation. Its effect scales with the displacement between the queried points, and its size is controlled through a half-mass Lipschitz condition on whole sample utilities.

descriptionHtml:
Spherical Random Utility Comparisons

We minimize a function f:Rd→R that is convex on the closed Euclidean ball K of radius R>0 centered at the origin, where d≥2. For each ordered pair in K, the oracle independently draws a spherically symmetric vector Z from a common law and reports whether the first point has at least as large a utility uZ(x)=f(x)+⟨Z,x⟩ as the second. With probability at least 1/2, uZ is B-Lipschitz on K, where B>0. The goal is a feasible output with integrable objective gap and expected gap at most ε, for 0<ε≤BR/16.

The optimization problem is minx∈Kf(x),K={x∈Rd:∥x∥2≤R}. The algorithm receives the integer dimension d, the radius R, the bound B, and the tolerance ε.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity on the ball). For every x,y∈K and t∈[0,1], f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y).

Assumption 2 (Spherical perturbations and Lipschitz utilities). The perturbation law μ is a probability measure on Rd. For every orthogonal transformation U and every Borel set A⊆Rd, it satisfies μ(U−1A)=μ(A). Define the set of perturbations G={z∈Rd:|uz(x)−uz(y)|≤B∥x−y∥2 for all x,y∈K}. Then μ(G)≥1/2.

For an ordered query (x,y)∈K×K, the comparison bit is c(x,y,z)=1{uz(y)≤uz(x)}. The map c is jointly measurable on K×K×Rd. On call k, the oracle returns c(x,y,Zk), where the Zk are independent random vectors with law μ and the entire sequence is independent of the algorithm’s randomness.

After the allotted calls, the algorithm must return x¯∈K. There must exist a minimizer x⋆∈argminx∈Kf(x) for which the gap f(x¯)−f(x⋆) is integrable and E[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε, where the expectation is over the algorithm’s randomness and the oracle perturbations.

theorems.formulaHtml: ⌈d⋅(672⋅B⋅Rε)2⌉+

theorems.referencesHtml:
• John C. Duchi, Michael I. Jordan, Martin J. Wainwright, and Andre Wibisono. Finite Sample Convergence Rates of Zero-Order Stochastic Optimization Methods. 2012. Complexity: Ω(dG2R2/ε2) adaptive same-sample paired-value calls for expected gap ε<cGR, where c>0 is universal. On the Gaussian linear hard instances, G bounds the root-mean-square sample slope norm. Taking G=B/2 ensures the required half-mass condition, and each value pair yields its comparison bit.
  • Evgeniy Kovalev, Fedor Stonyakin, and Alexander Gasnikov. Nonsmooth Convex and Strongly Convex Optimization from Noisy Comparisons. 2026 (arXiv v1). Complexity: Ω(d2σ2R2/ε2) adaptive binary comparisons for expected gap ε<cMR, where M is the objective Lipschitz bound, Z∼N(0,σ2Id), and c>0 is universal. On the radius-R ball, M=B/2 and σ=B/(22d) give admissible instances and Ω(dB2R2/ε2) comparisons.
theorems.formulaHtml: ⌊d⋅(B⋅Rε)2524288⌋+

comparisonHtml:
Let f be convex on the closed Euclidean ball Q of radius R>0 centered at zero in dimension d≥2. Each query (x,y)∈Q2 uses one fresh IID draw Z from an unknown spherically symmetric law and returns the jointly measurable bit 1{uZ(x)≥uZ(y)}, where uZ(x)=f(x)+⟨Z,x⟩. With probability at least 1/2, uZ is B-Lipschitz throughout Q. For B>0 and 0<ε≤BR/16, the target is a feasible x^ with integrable gap and E[f(x^)−minQf]≤ε.

Sufficient and necessary comparison budgets for spherical random utility.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) SphericalPreferenceDescent (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) Upper bound (sufficient)
O(d(BR/ε)2)
(2) SphericalPreferenceLowerBound (Ours) (review) Lower bound (necessary)
Ω(d(BR/ε)2) for randomized adaptive algorithms
(3) (Kovalev et al. 2026, Thm. 2(a)) Gaussian probit, convex Upper bound (sufficient)
O(1+(CdσR/ε)2)		 (1): Unknown spherical laws, including atoms and infinite means. No M, σ or link calibration. On the Gaussian ball, take B=M+σd. Matches (3) for σ≥M. For t=M/σ>1, the budget improves by a factor ≳t2min{d,t2}. At t=d, (1) costs O(d(MR/ε)2) versus at least order d3(MR/ε)2 in (3)’s budget. (1) needs a fixed horizon and a single envelope B. It covers balls only. (3) is anytime on convex bodies between concentric balls.
(4) (Kovalev et al. 2026, Thm. 2(a)) Gaussian probit, strongly convex Upper bound (sufficient)
O(1+min{(CdσRε)2,Cd2σ2με})		 (1) also covers nonsmooth convex objectives without positive curvature or Gaussian noise. (1) retains ε−2 dependence when 0<μ≤M/(8R), where (4) also gives an ε−1 bound.
(5) (Kovalev et al. 2026, Thm. 2(b)) Gaussian probit on the ball Lower bound (necessary)
Ω(d(BR/ε)2) for ε<BR/200, with M=B/2, σ=B/(4d)		 (2) formalizes the same order and extends it to BR/200≤ε≤BR/16, giving Ω(d) throughout that band for d≥2048. The full spherical class has matching upper and lower orders in (1), (2). (2) has a roughly 3.3 times smaller lower-bound coefficient for ε<BR/200.
(6) (Lu et al. 2026, Thm. 2) Online dueling No comparable expected-gap budget (1), (6): Rates are not comparable. (6) bounds query regret using an objective-gap link with known slope at zero. (1) compares utility differences whose noise scales with ∥x−y∥.
(7) (Saha et al. 2021) Noisy dueling No comparable spherical-noise budget (1), (7): Rates are not comparable under general spherical noise. (7) assumes smoothness and a constant probability of reversing the true preference.

Abbr: M is a Lipschitz bound for f, σ>0 the Gaussian standard deviation per coordinate, and μ the strong convexity modulus. C=C(M/σ) is the probit factor in Appendix B.1 of the paper cited in (3), with C(t)≥max{1,t2}.

Kovalev, Evgeniy, Fedor Stonyakin, and Alexander Gasnikov. 2026. Nonsmooth Convex and Strongly Convex Optimization from Noisy Comparisons. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2611.19611.
Lu, Yiyang, Hareshkumar Jadav, Mohammad Pedramfar, Ranveer Singh, and Vaneet Aggarwal. 2026. Online Convex Optimization with Dueling Feedback. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2608.15050.
Saha, Aadirupa, Tomer Koren, and Yishay Mansour. 2021. “Dueling Convex Optimization.” Proceedings of the 38th International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of machine learning research, vol. 139: 9245–54. https://proceedings.mlr.press/v139/saha21b.html.

import LongTails.Template
import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.MeasurableSpace
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.L1Space.Integrable

open MeasureTheory Set Metric
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace NNReal ENNReal

namespace LongTails.Setups.SphericalRandomUtility

open OracleTemplate

abbrev Point (d : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  R : ℝ≥0
  B : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

abbrev Feasible (p : Params) := closedBall (0 : Point p.d) p.R

noncomputable def sampleUtility {d : ℕ} (f : Point d → ℝ) (z x : Point d) : ℝ := f x + ⟪z, x⟫

def good (p : Params) (f : Point p.d → ℝ) : Set (Point p.d) :=
  {z | ∀ x y : Feasible p,
    |sampleUtility f z x - sampleUtility f z y| ≤ p.B * ‖(x : Point p.d) - y‖}

noncomputable def comparePair {p : Params} (f : Point p.d → ℝ)
    (q : Feasible p × Feasible p) (z : Point p.d) : Bool :=
  decide (sampleUtility f z q.2 ≤ sampleUtility f z q.1)

def Spherical {d : ℕ} (μ : Measure (Point d)) : Prop :=
  ∀ U : Point d ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Point d, μ.map U = μ

noncomputable abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  publicInput := id
  Query p := Feasible p × Feasible p
  Reply _ := Bool
  Output p := Feasible p
  Instance p := Point p.d → ℝ
  valid p := 2 ≤ p.d ∧ 0 < p.R ∧ 0 < p.B ∧ 0 < p.ε ∧ p.ε ≤ p.B * p.R / 16
  admissible p f O :=
    ConvexOn ℝ (closedBall (0 : Point p.d) p.R) f ∧
    Measurable (Function.uncurry (comparePair (p := p) f)) ∧
    ∃ (μ : ProbabilityMeasure (Point p.d)) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → Point p.d)),
      Spherical (d := p.d) (μ : Measure (Point p.d)) ∧ (1 / 2 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ (μ : Measure _) (good p f) ∧
      StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID (fun k (z : ℕ → Point p.d) => z k)
        (μ : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
      O = { Seed := fun _ => Point p.d
            law := P
            answer := fun _ (_, q) z => comparePair f q z }
  successful p f output P :=
    ∃ xstar : Feasible p, IsMinOn f (closedBall (0 : Point p.d) p.R) xstar.val ∧
      Integrable (fun z => f (output z).val - f xstar.val) (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ z, f (output z).val - f xstar.val ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.SphericalRandomUtility
